ways.label: Road end to Whataroa-Perth Track junction

end.name: Whataroa-Perth Track junction
end.quote: the junction of the Perth River and Whataroa River tracks is signposted

evidence: From the car park the track initially follows the 4WD track and markers up the true left bank.
A couple of boulder-hopping sections will see you passing opposite the Perth River confluence before reaching the Whataroa-Perth swing bridge.
Around 100m beyond the bridge the junction of the Perth River and Whataroa River tracks is signposted.

ways.label: Whataroa-Perth Track junction to Scone Hut
evidence: Whataroa-Perth Track junction – Scone Hut tramping track
The track then alternates between bush terraces and boulder hopping to Scone Hut (six bunks), with several notable side creeks needing to be crossed.

ways.label: Perth headwaters/Adams Wilderness Area access

end.name: end of marked track above Redfield swing bridge
end.quote: The marked track ends approximately 200 m above the Redfield swing bridge.

evidence: To access the Perth headwaters and Adams Wilderness Area from Scone Hut, follow the track across Lower Scone swing bridge, then to Redfield swing bridge.
The marked track ends approximately 200 m above the Redfield swing bridge.

ways.label: Scone Creek tramping track

start.name: Scone Hut
start.quote: Follow the track from the hut

end.name: small clearing downstream of the former Upper Scone swing bridge
end.quote: The marked track ends at the small clearing approximately 300 m downstream of the former Upper Scone swing bridge.

evidence: Follow the track from the hut past Lower Scone swing bridge (remaining on the true left of Scone Creek) upstream.
The marked track ends at the small clearing approximately 300 m downstream of the former Upper Scone swing bridge.

ways.label: Bettison Route

start.name: Scone Hut
start.quote: To access the Bettison Route from Scone Hut

end.name: two yellow and blue deer posts
end.quote: The marked route ends at the two yellow and blue deer posts.

evidence: To access the Bettison Route from Scone Hut follow the track upstream over Lower Scone swing bridge to the sign-posted junction.
The marked route ends at the two yellow and blue deer posts.

ways.label: Whataroa-Perth Track junction to Butler Junction Hut
evidence: The track to Butler Junction continues up the Whataroa valley with several short climbs before dropping steeply down to the beach downstream of The Twister.
Butler Junction Hut (eight bunks) is reached about ten minutes past McCormicks swing bridge.

ways.label: Butler Junction Hut to Whymper Hut
evidence: The track follows Butler River on the true right bank before crossing Butler Junction swing bridge.
The track then emerges onto an obvious open area towards the headwaters before climbing steeply up an old moraine wall on the true left to reach Whymper Hut (six bunks).

ways.label: Butler Junction Hut to Top Butler Hut

start.name: Butler Junction Hut
start.quote: From the hut the track follows the Butler River

evidence: From the hut the track follows the Butler River up the true right bank before crossing the swing bridge.
From here the track climbs and sidles across steep hillsides and creeks originating from King Peak, before reaching Top Butler Hut (six bunks).

ways.label: Top Butler to Ice Lake
evidence: Top Butler to Ice Lake tramping track
Boulder hop from here up to Ice Lake, where there are great views and small campsites.

not_on_route.name: Gunn Ridge Route
not_on_route.quote: Gunn Ridge Route is closed permanently because of severe erosion.

doubts: Page for a network of valley tracks, not one walk; each described track section is a way, W1 (road end section) listed first as main. No feature entries, so the car park (off SH6) and the Whataroa-Perth Track junction are unplaced. Shapes are recorded one_way as sections are described A to B; page does not say whether walkers return. W3-W5 are dead-end tracks from Scone Hut. Ford of The Twister is explicit; the Butler River (South Branch) bridge is destroyed and crossing on foot 'may be possible in low flow', recorded as a ford. Helicopter operators provide access to remote areas, but no place is named, so no exit/access point.
